On Sat, Dec 5, 2026 at 3:12 PM vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com wrote:
> Alex — thank you for the heads up and the logs. I’ve opened an incident ...

I've started live sampling. Early indicators:
- Elevated request queue depths in the request router for Folio tenant (avg queue depth 48 vs baseline 2).
- KV cache miss spike correlated with heavy prefix churn (many short-lived keys); memory churn + eviction is increasing tail latency.
- Continuous batching pipeline is building larger batches because backpressure from KV misses increases handler latency. That increases P95/P99 and then triggers timeouts upstream -> retry storms -> more load.

Immediate mitigations I can apply now (rolling):
1) Turn off continuous batching for the Folio route (will increase token cost but drop latency).
2) Apply conservative cache TTLs / disable aggressive prefix caching for the tenant.
3) Route Folio to a dedicated small pool (if capacity) or failover to smaller model variant.

I’m pushing a rollback of the most recent batching optimizer change to a narrow window to test — pushing now. I’ll attach trace snippets and perf dump to the bridge.

-Rishi
Sr. Director, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Alex — we see the same metrics on our side. I’ve temporarily disabled continuous batching for your tenant and disabled prefix aggregation on the cache. We are also throttling retry amplification by tightening the tenant circuit breaker.

What I did (15:50 PT):
- disabled continuous batching for tenant folio_123
- set cache prefix aggregation = false for folio_123
- applied stricter rate cap on retries (per-tenant)

Initial result: error rate dropped from 3.2% to 0.9% in about 8 minutes; P95 and P99 showed measurable improvement. We are monitoring for recurrence while we evaluate a longer-term fix.

Attachments: perf_dump_folio_20261205.tar.gz (diagnostic traces)

-Priyom

Mike / Alex — quick executive update:
- Mitigation applied (batching disabled + cache prefix aggregation off) at ~15:50 PT; error rate is back down below 1%.
- Our SRE/Product teams are treating this as Severity 1 and will produce a postmortem. Priyom is leading the technical write-up; Rishi is driving the runtime changes.
- For SLA credits: I’ve started the internal approval path; we aim to provide a preliminary credit estimate within 48 hours and a final proposal along with the postmortem.

- Root cause analysis (KV eviction + batching interaction causing queueing and retry amplification).
- Short-term: targeted config changes (we will re-enable controlled batching with stricter batch caps).
- Long-term: fix to batching optimizer logic to avoid enlarging batches under cache-thrash conditions; improved tenant-level circuit breakers and per-route isolation.

We will share the postmortem draft and a timeline for permanent remediation by Monday EOD. Thank you for patience and the clear incident playbook you provided.

Subject: Postmortem draft & status: Folio Health incident (504s)

Folks — attaching the initial postmortem draft and the perf dump I uploaded to Drive (link in thread). TL;DR: a recent change in the batching optimizer created a corner case where high KV-cache miss churn increased in-handler latency, which in turn increased batch window durations and created pathological queuing for the tenant; that queueing triggered more timeouts and upstream retries which amplified load until we disabled batching.

Status now:
- Fix branch created for the batching optimizer; test-run scheduled tonight in staging with synthetic cache-thrash patterns.
- Plan to re-enable controlled batching with conservative caps for Folio on Mon 12/7 after validation.
- Postmortem draft (slo_postmortem_draft_folio.md) shared for review — owners: Priyom (technical), Vanessa (customer comms), Lauren (legal/credits).

I’ll update the HubSpot deal and attach the final postmortem after review.

-Priyom
